response:
Prior evidence lesson: both accepted gen-0 signals had very low coverage (~0.11) and weak portfolio evidence despite a decent FMB t-stat on the conditional capex signal. Two fixes drive this batch: (a) the validator requires a theme-exclusive variable from each side, so every expression below contains one of {capx, ppent, ppegt, invt, emp, aqc, sstk} and one of {xrd, xad, sale, cogs, ceq}; (b) `COALESCE(xrd, 0)` did not rescue coverage, so I stop relying on it and instead include two high-coverage mechanisms that proxy the intangible franchise with margin/revenue-productivity variables, alongside R&D-based signals whose coverage limitation is accepted but whose economics are sharper.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Commodity_Capacity_Expansion
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(GROWTH(capx, 1), NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(SUB(sale, cogs), sale))))
HYPOTHESIS: Physical capacity expansion is value-destroying precisely where the firm has no intangible moat; gross margin (industry-adjusted) proxies for brand/technology-based pricing power, so capex growth by low-margin commodity producers signals overinvestment into competitive erosion.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: The gen-0 conditional capex signal had the right cross-sectional sign but a broken long-short leg partly because a hard indicator threw away half the cross-section and R&D reporting truncated coverage to 12%; replacing the R&D screen with an industry-adjusted gross-margin rank keeps nearly the full universe and grades the intangible franchise continuously. The interaction is essential: high capex growth in high-margin franchises is capacity for rents, while the same growth in low-margin firms is capital destruction.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Self_Financed_Research
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(xrd, sale), NEG(RATIO(sstk, at)))
HYPOTHESIS: Research intensity is rewarded only when it is funded from internal cash flow; R&D funded by fresh equity issuance reflects speculative, cash-burning innovation that the market overprices, whereas internally funded research is conservatively expensed and underpriced.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This introduces a financing channel absent from the archive: the same R&D intensity carries opposite information depending on whether the firm must sell stock to pay for it, which links the investment theme (external equity financing) to the intangibles theme (knowledge spending). It should also stabilize the short leg, since issuance-heavy R&D firms are a well-defined, persistently underperforming group rather than an unstable residual.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Bought_vs_Built_Innovation
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(aqc, at), NEG(RATIO(xrd, sale)))
HYPOTHESIS: Firms that acquire their intangible capital through cash acquisitions pay a control premium and face integration risk, while firms that build it internally through R&D understate book value and earnings; buying rather than building innovation predicts low returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: This repairs the rejected gen-0 "bought vs built" idea by using the investment-exclusive acquisition flow (aqc) instead of goodwill, which the validator treats as a shared variable. The two legs contrast two economically substitutable routes to the same intangible stock, so the spread is a pure "make-or-buy" portfolio rather than a restatement of the acquisition anomaly.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Asset_Light_Production_Mix
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(RATIO(intan, sale), NEG(RATIO(ppegt, sale)))
HYPOTHESIS: Holding revenue scale fixed, firms that generate sales from recognized intangible capital rather than from gross physical plant have lower operating leverage, higher scalability, and are systematically underpriced relative to capital-heavy competitors.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This tests a stock (production-mix) mechanism rather than the flow/growth mechanisms dominating the archive, and by scaling both asset classes by sales it isolates composition instead of size or growth. Coverage should be high because intan, ppegt, and sale are broadly reported, giving a cleaner read on whether the tangible-versus-intangible distinction pays at the level rather than the change.
INTERACTION_TYPE: ratio

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Headcount_Growth_Without_Knowledge_Deepening
EXPRESSION: SUMRANK(GROWTH(emp, 1), NEG(GROWTH(RATIO(xrd, emp), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: Labor expansion that dilutes R&D per employee reflects scale-chasing in low-skill capacity, whereas hiring accompanied by rising research spend per worker reflects genuine human-capital deepening; the former predicts low returns.
EXPECTED_SIGN: negative
REASONING: Employment growth is an investment margin that no archive signal has touched, and interacting it with knowledge intensity per worker separates "more bodies" from "better capital per body." The mechanism is a change concept by construction, since the economics concern the direction in which the workforce mix is being reshaped rather than its level.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Knowledge_Share_Reallocation_Trend
EXPRESSION: TREND(RATIO(xrd, ADD(xrd, capx)), 5)
HYPOTHESIS: A multi-year drift of the investment budget away from physical capex and toward research reflects a durable strategic reallocation toward intangible production; because expensed R&D depresses current earnings while capex is capitalized, this transition mechanically worsens accounting profitability and is underpriced.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Gen-0's one-year acceleration version of this idea was directionally right but statistically weak (t=1.31), consistent with single-year investment mix changes being dominated by noise; a five-year trend in the knowledge share extracts the persistent component of the same economic channel. The ratio form also avoids the scale dependence of separately ranked legs and keeps the signal defined for any firm that reports both spending categories.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel
